Q000251:
Why this is correct:
Amazon MSK ingests high-throughput streams and lets the team reuse existing Kafka tools, clients, and connectors.

Why the other options are wrong:
• SQS: queue, not Kafka.
• DMS: database migration.
• Kinesis: different API, can't reuse Kafka tooling.

Key takeaway: reuse Kafka ecosystem → MSK.
Q000256:
Why this is correct:
An EventBridge schedule invokes the function periodically, replacing a costly sleep loop that pays for idle time.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Longer timeout with sleep: still wasteful.
• RDS stored procedure: wrong tool.
• Transfer Acceleration: unrelated.

Key takeaway: periodic polling → schedules, not sleep loops.
Q000258:
Why this is correct:
A larger batch size and the parallelization factor (multiple concurrent batches per shard) increase Lambda throughput from Kinesis.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Fewer shards: less throughput.
• Less memory: slower.
• Standard throughput only: doesn't add parallelism.

Key takeaway: Lambda lag on Kinesis → batch size + parallelization factor.
Q000259:
Why this is correct:
Throughput exceptions mean producers exceed shard limits. Add shards or use on-demand mode, and implement exponential backoff and retries in producers.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Shorter retention: unrelated.
• Disable encryption: unrelated.
• Omit partition key: required.

Key takeaway: write throttling → capacity + backoff.
Q000260:
Why this is correct:
Enhanced fan-out gives each registered consumer its own 2 MB/s per-shard read throughput, so many consumers don't compete.

Why the other options are wrong:
• On-demand: write capacity.
• KMS encryption: security.
• Firehose: delivery.

Key takeaway: many consumers → enhanced fan-out.
Q000262:
Why this is correct:
Retention beyond 24 hours (up to 365 days) costs extra per shard-hour, and longer-term retention adds per-GB charges.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Deletes after 7 days: configurable.
• No cost: extra cost applies.
• Requires recreating the stream: no.

Key takeaway: replay window costs money.
Q000264:
Why this is correct:
Assigning the replication instance a fixed private IP (or using its static private address) lets the on-premises firewall allow it reliably over DX or VPN.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Rotate IP daily: breaks rules.
• Transfer Acceleration: S3 only.
• Disable security groups: unsafe.

Key takeaway: stable IPs for firewall rules.
Q000265:
Why this is correct:
Redshift streaming ingestion reads Kinesis directly into a materialized view with low latency, without staging in S3.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Federated query to RDS: not streams.
• Snapshot restore: backups.
• Spectrum: S3 data.

Key takeaway: stream into Redshift → streaming ingestion.
Q000268:
Why this is correct:
Exponential backoff with jitter, honoring the API's Retry-After or rate limits, avoids overwhelming a rate-limited API.

Why the other options are wrong:
• More concurrency: more rate limit errors.
• Change trigger: unrelated.
• Disable retries: loses data.

Key takeaway: rate-limited APIs → backoff with jitter.
Q000269:
Why this is correct:
Glue job bookmarks track processed data so each run handles only new files.

Why the other options are wrong:
• DynamicFrame partitioning: layout.
• Catalog versioning: schema history.
• Worker type: capacity.

Key takeaway: incremental processing → job bookmarks.
Q000270:
Why this is correct:
Amazon EKS runs containerized Spark with Kubernetes-native scheduling and tooling (EMR on EKS is another option).

Why the other options are wrong:
• EMR Serverless: no Kubernetes.
• Lambda: not for Spark.
• ECS Fargate: not Kubernetes.

Key takeaway: Kubernetes-native Spark → EKS.
Q000273:
Why this is correct:
A Glue job can define multiple connections and create DynamicFrames from Redshift and other sources, then join them in one job.

Why the other options are wrong:
• S3 Batch Operations: object actions.
• Two Lambdas: limited and complex.
• Spectrum only: doesn't join external sources this way.

Key takeaway: multi-source ETL in one Glue job.
Q000274:
Why this is correct:
Glue Flex execution runs non-urgent jobs on spare capacity at lower cost, with variable start times.

Why the other options are wrong:
• G.2X: capacity.
• Bookmarks: incremental.
• More DPUs: more cost.

Key takeaway: non-urgent Glue jobs → Flex.
Q000278:
Why this is correct:
Mixed structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data arriving at varying rates means high variety and variable velocity.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Low variety: incorrect.
• Single type: incorrect.
• Low volume constant velocity: incorrect.

Key takeaway: characterize data by volume, velocity, and variety.
Q000279:
Why this is correct:
Bedrock foundation models can extract structured entities from unstructured text within a pipeline.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Kinesis Analytics: stream SQL.
• Schema Registry: schemas.
• Spectrum: S3 queries.

Key takeaway: entity extraction from text → FMs via Bedrock (or Comprehend).
Q000280:
Why this is correct:
Glue DynamicFrames handle inconsistent or evolving schemas with choice types, without failing.

Why the other options are wrong:
• NumPy arrays: no.
• Standard DataFrame: needs fixed schema.
• Pandas: not distributed.

Key takeaway: messy schemas in Glue → DynamicFrame.
Q000281:
Why this is correct:
Partitioning by year, month, and country in the S3 path lets Athena prune partitions for common filters.

Why the other options are wrong:
• File size: not a filter.
• UUID: useless for pruning.
• Unpartitioned: full scans.

Key takeaway: partition by common filter columns.
Q000282:
Why this is correct:
EMR Serverless removes cluster management and scales automatically for sporadic jobs.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Identical control: EC2 gives more control.
• Serverless needs provisioning: reversed.
• EC2 can't run Spark: false.

Key takeaway: sporadic Spark → EMR Serverless.
Q000283:
Why this is correct:
A JDBC connection timeout from Glue usually means the job's subnet lacks a route or security group rule to reach RDS.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Driver newer: different error.
• Multi-AZ: unrelated.
• Catalog name mismatch: different error.

Key takeaway: Glue connection timeouts → networking.
Q000285:
Why this is correct:
Many tiny files add per-file overhead. Compact them into larger files, or use Glue's file grouping options.

Why the other options are wrong:
• JSON: no help.
• Disable bookmarks: no help.
• More DPUs: treats symptom.

Key takeaway: small files → compaction/grouping.
Q000286:
Why this is correct:
The Redshift Data API runs SQL asynchronously over HTTPS without managing connections or drivers.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Spectrum: S3 queries.
• JDBC pool in Lambda: connection management.
• RDS Proxy: not for Redshift.

Key takeaway: HTTP SQL to Redshift → Data API.
Q000289:
Why this is correct:
An EventBridge rule matching the custom event can start the Step Functions state machine.

Why the other options are wrong:
• SNS only: no direct pattern routing to Step Functions in this way.
• SSM Automation: not an event router.
• Config: compliance.

Key takeaway: event-driven orchestration → EventBridge.
Q000290:
Why this is correct:
A single orchestrating Lambda is bounded by the 15-minute maximum execution time, so long pipelines fail. Step Functions avoids this.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Step Functions can't invoke Lambda: it can.
• No data passing: possible but not the main limit.
• Lambda can't invoke Lambda: it can.

Key takeaway: orchestration beyond 15 minutes → Step Functions.
Q000291:
Why this is correct:
Express Workflows are designed for high-volume, short-duration executions at low cost.

Why the other options are wrong:
• EC2 activity workers: heavy.
• Standard: costly at this volume.
• Zero-second wait: meaningless.

Key takeaway: millions of short workflows → Express.
Q000292:
Why this is correct:
A Retry field with interval, backoff rate, and max attempts handles transient errors, and a Catch routes persistent failures.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Parallel without handling: no.
• More memory: doesn't fix transient failures.
• Empty Map: no.

Key takeaway: transient failures → Retry + Catch.
Q000295:
Why this is correct:
A conditional trigger with AND logic fires the downstream job only after both crawlers succeed.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Scheduled trigger: ignores dependencies.
• On-demand: manual.
• Bookmarks: incremental data.

Key takeaway: dependencies in Glue workflows → conditional triggers.
Q000296:
Why this is correct:
A dead-letter queue (such as SQS) on the EventBridge target captures events that fail after retries.

Why the other options are wrong:
• S3 versioning: unrelated.
• Disable retries: loses events.
• Longer timeout: doesn't capture failures.

Key takeaway: capture failed events → DLQ.
Q000297:
Why this is correct:
MWAA runs across multiple AZs and automatically scales workers within the configured minimum and maximum.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Fixed workers: it autoscales.
• Manual EC2: no.
• No AZ redundancy: it has it.

Key takeaway: MWAA autoscaling is built in.
Q000299:
Why this is correct:
For a small number of infrequent workflows, Step Functions is serverless with no always-on environment cost. MWAA has a minimum environment cost.

Why the other options are wrong:
• MWAA no minimum cost: false.
• Step Functions needs Python DAGs: no.
• MWAA cheaper for small workflows: no.

Key takeaway: light orchestration → Step Functions.
Q000301:
Why this is correct:
An SQS queue delivers a message to one consumer system, decoupling stages.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Pinpoint: marketing messages.
• Events with no target: nothing happens.
• SNS with no subscriber: nothing delivered.

Key takeaway: notify one consumer reliably → SQS.
Q000302:
Why this is correct:
Vectorized operations (pandas or NumPy) or joins replace slow Python loops over large lists.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Longer timeout: still slow.
• More prints: slower.
• Recursion: slower and risky.

Key takeaway: slow loops → vectorize.
Q000303:
Why this is correct:
Provisioned concurrency keeps environments initialized, avoiding cold starts during spikes.

Why the other options are wrong:
• X-Ray: observation.
• Longer timeout: unrelated.
• Reserved concurrency 1: throttles.

Key takeaway: cold starts → provisioned concurrency.
Q000304:
Why this is correct:
Lambda allocates CPU in proportion to memory. Increasing memory gives CPU-bound functions more CPU.

Why the other options are wrong:
• More layers: packaging.
• Less memory: slower.
• Longer timeout: doesn't speed up.

Key takeaway: CPU-bound Lambda → more memory.
Q000307:
Why this is correct:
Extracting transformation logic into plain functions lets you unit test them locally (for example, with pytest and a local Spark session) without running the whole Glue job.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Inspect S3 output manually: not unit tests.
• Run against production catalog: risky.
• Disable bookmarks: unrelated.

Key takeaway: testable ETL → separate logic from I/O.
Q000311:
Why this is correct:
An EFS file system mounted via Lambda's file system configuration provides shared, persistent, read-write storage across invocations.

Why the other options are wrong:
• /tmp only: per environment, not shared.
• Instance store: not accessible.
• Deep Archive: slow.

Key takeaway: shared Lambda file storage → EFS.
Q000312:
Why this is correct:
CodePipeline orchestrating CodeBuild to run tests and deploy scripts automates Glue ETL CI/CD.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Manual uploads: no automation.
• Macie: data scanning.
• Config rules on commits: no.

Key takeaway: ETL CI/CD → CodePipeline + CodeBuild.
Q000313:
Why this is correct:
A shuffle redistributes data across partitions (for example, by join key) during wide operations like joins.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Checkpointing: state saving.
• Garbage collection: memory.
• Broadcast: avoids shuffles for small tables.

Key takeaway: joins across partitions → shuffle.
Q000314:
Why this is correct:
A hash set gives average constant-time membership checks for record IDs.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Unbalanced tree: slow.
• Sorted array linear scan: slow.
• Linked list: slow.

Key takeaway: fast lookups → hash structures.
Q000315:
Why this is correct:
S3 events can be delivered more than once. Idempotent processing (for example, recording processed object keys or version IDs) prevents duplicate effects.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Reserved concurrency: doesn't dedupe.
• Smaller payload: no.
• Stateless only: doesn't prevent duplicates.

Key takeaway: at-least-once events → idempotency.
Q000318:
Why this is correct:
MemoryDB for Redis is a durable in-memory database with microsecond reads and Multi-AZ durability.

Why the other options are wrong:
• DynamoDB + DAX: microsecond reads, but writes aren't in-memory latency.
• Memcached: not durable.
• Aurora: not microsecond.

Key takeaway: durable in-memory key-value → MemoryDB.
Q000319:
Why this is correct:
MSK runs Apache Kafka, so existing native Kafka clients work without code changes.

Why the other options are wrong:
• SQS, Kinesis, Firehose: different APIs.

Key takeaway: existing Kafka clients → MSK.
Q000320:
Why this is correct:
pgvector's HNSW index enables fast approximate nearest-neighbor similarity search on embeddings.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Hash, GIN, B-tree: not vector similarity indexes.

Key takeaway: vector similarity in Aurora → HNSW.
Q000321:
Why this is correct:
IVF needs a training (clustering) step before indexing and is lighter on memory. HNSW builds a graph with better recall and query speed but uses more memory.

Why the other options are wrong:
• IVF exact only: it's approximate.
• HNSW builds faster with less memory: generally the opposite.
• Identical: no.

Key takeaway: HNSW = recall/speed; IVF = lighter, needs training.
Q000323:
Why this is correct:
Redshift federated query joins Redshift tables with live data in RDS or Aurora PostgreSQL/MySQL in one query.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Spectrum: S3.
• Materialized views: precomputed.
• Athena: separate engine.

Key takeaway: query operational DBs from Redshift → federated query.
Q000325:
Why this is correct:
Redshift Spectrum queries Parquet files in S3 directly through external tables.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Federated query: operational databases.
• Glue crawler: cataloging.
• Athena federated query: separate engine.

Key takeaway: S3 data from Redshift → Spectrum.
Q000326:
Why this is correct:
A long-running open transaction holding a lock blocks VACUUM and COPY. Find it in the system tables (such as STV_LOCKS) and end it.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Max rows: no.
• WLM zero slots: not the symptom.
• Auto-resolved: no.

Key takeaway: hanging Redshift jobs → lock contention.
Q000327:
Why this is correct:
Apache Iceberg adds ACID transactions, schema evolution, and time travel to data lake tables.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Parquet and ORC: file formats only.
• CSV with manifests: no ACID.

Key takeaway: transactional data lake tables → Iceberg.
Q000328:
Why this is correct:
Partition key CustomerID with sort key OrderDate lets one Query return a customer's orders sorted by date.

Why the other options are wrong:
• OrderID only: can't query by customer.
• Date as partition: wrong grouping.
• Random UUID: no access pattern.

Key takeaway: design keys for the access pattern.
Q000330:
Why this is correct:
Lake Formation enforces fine-grained table, column, and row permissions on data cataloged in Glue.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Crawlers: discovery.
• S3 IAM only: no column-level control.
• Macie: discovery.

Key takeaway: fine-grained data lake permissions → Lake Formation.
Q000332:
Why this is correct:
Configuring EMR to use the Glue Data Catalog as its external Hive metastore keeps metadata persistent and shared across clusters and services.

Why the other options are wrong:
• RDS metastore rewrite: unnecessary.
• DynamoDB metadata: no.
• Local metastore: lost with clusters.

Key takeaway: shared Hive metastore → Glue Data Catalog.
Q000334:
Why this is correct:
New partitions must be registered in the Glue Data Catalog (via crawler, MSCK REPAIR, ALTER TABLE, or partition projection) before Athena sees them.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Versioning: unrelated.
• Deleted role: would fail entirely.
• Athena doesn't support partitions: it does.

Key takeaway: new partitions → register or use projection.
Q000336:
Why this is correct:
Classifiers inferring slightly different schemas create new table versions. Configure the crawler's schema change policy or custom classifiers.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Can't change: configurable.
• Athena doesn't support versioning: unrelated.
• S3 versioning: unrelated.

Key takeaway: schema flapping → crawler configuration.
Q000337:
Why this is correct:
Crawling hourly when data changes monthly incurs unnecessary crawler charges. Schedule to match the data or trigger on change.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Required hourly: no.
• Can't schedule less: can.
• No charges: they're charged.
• Deletes table: no.

Key takeaway: match crawler schedule to data changes.
Q000338:
Why this is correct:
Registering the data in Lake Formation and granting table and column permissions gives read-only access to exactly what's needed.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Copy bucket policies: no column control.
• Separate catalog: duplication.
• Full bucket access: over-privileged.

Key takeaway: table/column access → Lake Formation grants.
Q000341:
Why this is correct:
An S3 Lifecycle policy with transitions moves logs to cheaper classes as access declines, and can expire them later.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Object Lock: retention.
• Transfer Acceleration: speed.
• CRR: replication.

Key takeaway: declining access → lifecycle transitions.
Q000343:
Why this is correct:
S3 Versioning keeps previous versions, so overwritten objects can be recovered.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Transfer Acceleration, Intelligent-Tiering, Requester Pays: unrelated.

Key takeaway: recover overwrites → versioning.
Q000344:
Why this is correct:
Object Lock in Compliance mode prevents deletion or overwriting of locked versions until retention expires, even by administrators. The data can't be deleted early.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Current version only: applies per version.
• Versioning disables Object Lock: no.
• Admins can bypass: not in compliance mode.

Key takeaway: compliance mode is absolute until expiry.
Q000345:
Why this is correct:
UNLOAD with parallel output (the default) and a columnar format such as Parquet writes multiple files quickly and efficiently for downstream use.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Single CSV: slow.
• Disable compression: larger output.
• Lambda INSERTs: impractical.

Key takeaway: large exports → parallel UNLOAD to Parquet.
Q000346:
Why this is correct:
Cross-Region Replication keeps copies in another Region, so data stays available during a Regional outage.

Why the other options are wrong:
• SRR: same Region.
• Expiration: deletes.
• S3 Select: queries.

Key takeaway: Regional resilience → CRR.
Q000347:
Why this is correct:
Automated and manual snapshots let you restore a Redshift cluster or table to a previous point.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Materialized views: performance.
• Concurrency scaling: performance.
• Spectrum: S3 queries.

Key takeaway: Redshift recovery → snapshots.
Q000348:
Why this is correct:
Each object transitioned to a Glacier class incurs a per-object transition charge, plus per-object metadata overhead, so many small objects can cost more.

Why the other options are wrong:
• No fees: false.
• Can't apply to small objects: false.
• Small objects deleted: false.

Key takeaway: lifecycle transitions cost per object.
Q000349:
Why this is correct:
DynamoDB Point-in-Time Recovery restores to any second within the last 35 days.

Why the other options are wrong:
• On-demand backups only: fixed points.
• Streams: 24-hour change log.
• Global Tables: replication.

Key takeaway: any-point restore → PITR.
Q000350:
Why this is correct:
In a versioned bucket, expiring the current version adds a delete marker; the previous version becomes noncurrent and remains unless a noncurrent expiration rule removes it.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Disables versioning: no.
• Ignores rules: no.
• Deletes all versions: no.

Key takeaway: versioned expiration → delete markers + noncurrent versions.
Q000351:
Why this is correct:
Setting the distribution key to customer_id on both tables co-locates joined rows on the same slices, avoiding data redistribution.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Sort key only: doesn't collocate.
• Unused sort key: no benefit.
• No keys: may redistribute.

Key takeaway: frequent joins → matching distribution keys.
Q000352:
Why this is correct:
Defining clear, well-organized schemas in the Glue Data Catalog (with sensitive columns identifiable, and tags if needed) lets Lake Formation apply column-level and tag-based permissions.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Mixing sensitive columns without structure: harder to govern.
• Single shared key: no fine-grained control.
• Separate account with no access model: impractical.

Key takeaway: governable schemas enable fine-grained control.
Q000353:
Why this is correct:
A low-cardinality partition key concentrates traffic. Redesign with a higher-cardinality key (for example, order ID or composite keys).

Why the other options are wrong:
• GSI with same key: same hot spot.
• Reduce reads: unrelated.
• Billing mode switch: doesn't fix hot keys.

Key takeaway: hot partitions → higher-cardinality keys.
Q000355:
Why this is correct:
DMS Schema Conversion is a managed, console-integrated feature for converting schemas within DMS, alongside data migration.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Unrelated tools: they overlap.
• SCT migrates live data: DMS does.
• Same-engine only: supports heterogeneous.

Key takeaway: schema + data in DMS → DMS Schema Conversion.
Q000357:
Why this is correct:
SageMaker Catalog integrates with lineage tracking, so business users can see where data came from and how it was transformed, not just its schema.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Only names and types: it shows more.
• Manual free-text lineage: no.
• Only raw Glue views: no.

Key takeaway: trust in data → surface lineage in the catalog.
Q000358:
Why this is correct:
Partitioning the data and table by event_date lets Athena skip files outside the filter, scanning less data.

Why the other options are wrong:
• GSI on S3: doesn't exist.
• One huge file: hurts parallelism.
• Uncompressed CSV: slower.

Key takeaway: frequent date filters → partition by date.
Q000359:
Why this is correct:
Applying suitable column encodings (for example, AZ64 or ZSTD, or ENCODE AUTO) shrinks storage and I/O, speeding queries.

Why the other options are wrong:
• More nodes: costs more without fixing encoding.
• Convert to view: no storage.
• Disable compression: worse.

Key takeaway: Redshift storage → column encodings.
Q000360:
Why this is correct:
A Redshift sort key physically orders data on disk so zone maps skip blocks. A DynamoDB GSI is a separate index with its own keys for a different access pattern.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Identical: no.
• GSI reorders base table: no.
• Sort key changed at query time: no.

Key takeaway: sort key = physical order; GSI = alternate access path.
Q000362:
Why this is correct:
Denormalization stores related data together for fast single-request reads, at the cost of duplicated data and more complex updates.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Only affects writes: affects reads too.
• No downsides: there are.
• Not possible: common practice.

Key takeaway: DynamoDB denormalization trades update complexity for read speed.
Q000364:
Why this is correct:
Queued tasks mean there aren't enough workers. Increase the environment class or maximum worker count.

Why the other options are wrong:
• S3 versioning: unrelated.
• Shorter schedule: more load.
• Earlier start_date: backfills more.

Key takeaway: queued Airflow tasks → more worker capacity.
Q000366:
Why this is correct:
Paginated APIs require looping and passing the returned nextToken until no token remains.

Why the other options are wrong:
• API Gateway merging: no.
• Longer timeout: doesn't stop pagination.
• Single call: misses data.

Key takeaway: paginated APIs → loop on nextToken.
Q000369:
Why this is correct:
CTAS creates a new permanent table in the Glue Data Catalog from a query's results, with chosen format and location.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Named query: stored SQL text.
• Saved query: stored SQL text.
• UNLOAD: writes files without a table.

Key takeaway: new table from a query → CTAS.
Q000371:
Why this is correct:
Enable S3 EventBridge notifications, then create a rule matching the object key pattern that starts the state machine.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Polling every 5 minutes: delayed.
• Config then manual start: slow.
• SNS email: manual.

Key takeaway: S3 events → EventBridge → Step Functions.
Q000373:
Why this is correct:
Data Wrangler provides visual exploration, target leakage detection, and quick model analysis for ML data preparation.

Why the other options are wrong:
• DataBrew: general prep without ML insights.
• Athena: queries.
• QuickSight: dashboards.

Key takeaway: ML data exploration → Data Wrangler.
Q000375:
Why this is correct:
GROUP BY region with SUM computes totals per region, and HAVING keeps only regions whose total exceeds the threshold.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Only the highest region: no.
• HAVING with aggregate errors: it's valid.
• Individual rows: HAVING filters groups.

Key takeaway: HAVING filters aggregated groups.
Q000376:
Why this is correct:
AVG(...) OVER (ORDER BY sale_date ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) computes a 7-day rolling average per row.

Why the other options are wrong:
• PARTITION BY date: averages within each date.
• No OVER: single value.
• GROUP BY date: no rolling window.

Key takeaway: rolling metrics → window frames.
Q000378:
Why this is correct:
Redshift Serverless scales compute automatically and charges for usage, fitting unpredictable workloads.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Fixed cluster for peak: idle cost.
• Pause nightly: doesn't fit variable weeks.
• EMR Presto: replaces the warehouse.

Key takeaway: unpredictable analytics → Redshift Serverless.
Q000379:
Why this is correct:
A pivot turns row values (months) into columns, one row per product.

Why the other options are wrong:
• GROUP BY without aggregate: no reshaping.
• UNION ALL: stacks rows.
• Self join: not pivoting.

Key takeaway: rows to columns → pivot.
Q000384:
Why this is correct:
Executor out-of-memory errors call for more workers or a larger worker type (such as G.2X) with more memory per executor.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Python shell: less power.
• Shorter timeout: unrelated.
• AdministratorAccess: unrelated.

Key takeaway: Glue OOM → bigger or more workers.
Q000385:
Why this is correct:
Keep Spot on task nodes only, which hold no HDFS data. Master and core nodes stay On-Demand so interruptions don't lose data.

Why the other options are wrong:
• HDFS on Spot: data loss.
• Disable health checks: hides failures.
• Spot master: cluster loss.

Key takeaway: EMR Spot → task nodes only.
Q000386:
Why this is correct:
CloudWatch Logs Insights can count ERROR entries per 5-minute bin with stats count(*) by bin(5m).

Why the other options are wrong:
• Trusted Advisor: no.
• Copy to S3 for Athena: unnecessary.
• X-Ray map: traces.

Key takeaway: time-bucketed log counts → Logs Insights.
Q000387:
Why this is correct:
Athena queries both log sets directly in S3 with SQL, including joins, using tables over the partitioned paths.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Trusted Advisor, CloudTrail Insights, Inspector: not log query tools.

Key takeaway: ad hoc SQL on S3 logs → Athena.
Q000389:
Why this is correct:
Slow ad hoc queries during busy periods often come from queueing. Review and adjust WLM queues, concurrency, or enable concurrency scaling.

Why the other options are wrong:
• S3 versioning: unrelated.
• Stored procedures: no.
• Read replicas: not a Redshift feature.

Key takeaway: query queueing → WLM tuning.
Q000391:
Why this is correct:
A Glue Data Quality ruleset in DQDL (for example, a completeness threshold) can fail the job when too many values are null.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Redshift CHECK constraints: not enforced.
• Crawler rejects: no.
• Manual inspection: no automation.

Key takeaway: automated quality gates → Glue Data Quality.
Q000392:
Why this is correct:
A DataBrew profile job shows value distributions and unexpected values in the column.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Delete column: loses data.
• Bigger sample without profiling: no insight.
• Export unmodified: no check.

Key takeaway: inspect column values → profiling.
Q000393:
Why this is correct:
Stratified sampling preserves the proportions of groups in the sample, so the profile represents the full dataset.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Last 24 hours only: biased.
• Full dataset every time: slow.
• First 500 rows: biased.

Key takeaway: representative samples → stratified sampling.
Q000395:
Why this is correct:
Salting adds a random suffix to skewed keys, spreading their rows across partitions (with a matching salted join).

Why the other options are wrong:
• Single partition: no parallelism.
• Disable speculation: doesn't fix skew.
• Fewer executors: slower.

Key takeaway: key skew → salting.
Q000396:
Why this is correct:
The rule fails because 92% of values passing is below the configured threshold.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Rounds up: no.
• Ruleset skipped: no.
• Halts monitoring: no.

Key takeaway: quality rules compare pass rates to thresholds.
Q000399:
Why this is correct:
A gateway VPC endpoint for S3, with an endpoint policy, keeps S3 traffic on the AWS network without the internet.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Internet gateway: internet.
• NAT gateway: internet path.
• Inbound SG rule: irrelevant.

Key takeaway: private S3 access → gateway endpoint.
Q000400:
Why this is correct:
A resource-based permission on the Lambda function lets API Gateway invoke it.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Make public: insecure.
• IAM user keys: insecure.
• VPC peering: irrelevant.

Key takeaway: service-to-Lambda → resource-based policy.
Q000402:
Why this is correct:
Enabling trusted access for CloudFormation StackSets in Organizations allows service-managed StackSets to deploy baselines across member accounts.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Bucket policy: unrelated.
• Replicated secret: unrelated.
• Config aggregator: read-only.

Key takeaway: org-wide stack deployment → StackSets trusted access.
Q000403:
Why this is correct:
In SageMaker Unified Studio, a domain contains domain units, and domain units contain projects where members collaborate.

Why the other options are wrong:
• S3 policies only: no.
• Projects contain domains: reversed.
• Single global namespace: no.

Key takeaway: domain → domain units → projects.
Q000404:
Why this is correct:
A custom IAM policy allowing only the required Athena actions, workgroup, Glue tables, and S3 locations gives least privilege.

Why the other options are wrong:
• AdministratorAccess: excessive.
• AthenaFullAccess: broad.
• Root access: never.

Key takeaway: least privilege → custom scoped policy.
Q000406:
Why this is correct:
ABAC using resource tags applies permissions automatically to any bucket carrying the matching tag.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Bucket ACLs: manual.
• Fixed ARN lists: need updates.
• Security groups: not for S3.

Key takeaway: automatic access by tags → ABAC.
Q000407:
Why this is correct:
RBAC can lead to role and policy sprawl as teams grow, requiring many updates. ABAC scales via tags.

Why the other options are wrong:
• RBAC inherits tags: no.
• ABAC impossible in IAM: false.
• RBAC needs no management: false.

Key takeaway: RBAC sprawl vs. ABAC scale.
Q000409:
Why this is correct:
For Lake Formation-governed tables, the role needs both IAM permissions and Lake Formation grants on the table.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Deleted bucket: different error.
• Invalid JSON: policy wouldn't save.
• Athena unsupported: it's supported.

Key takeaway: governed tables need Lake Formation grants.
Q000410:
Why this is correct:
With SSE-KMS, the KMS key policy must allow the principal to use the key, and IAM policies must also permit it where the key policy delegates.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Only key policy: IAM also matters.
• IAM alone: key policy required.
• Bucket policy alone: no.

Key takeaway: KMS access = key policy + IAM.
Q000411:
Why this is correct:
A bucket policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false forces HTTPS for all requests.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Endpoint policy only: doesn't cover all paths.
• SSE-S3: at rest.
• Versioning: unrelated.

Key takeaway: enforce TLS → SecureTransport deny.
Q000413:
Why this is correct:
Account B's role needs kms:Decrypt granted in Account A's key policy (plus its own IAM permission and bucket access).

Why the other options are wrong:
• Works by default: no.
• Copy the key: impossible.
• Bucket policy only: KMS also needed.

Key takeaway: cross-account SSE-KMS → key policy grant.
Q000415:
Why this is correct:
If an alias was re-pointed to a new key, new data is encrypted with the new key. Decrypt failures suggest the app lacks permission on the new key (or old data still needs the old key).

Why the other options are wrong:
• Secrets rotation: unrelated.
• KMS re-encrypts objects: no.
• Old key material deleted: no.

Key takeaway: alias changes switch the key used.
Q000416:
Why this is correct:
Macie discovers PII in S3, and Redshift dynamic data masking hides sensitive values from query results by role.

Why the other options are wrong:
• CloudTrail discovery: no.
• GuardDuty discovery: no.
• Config discovery: no.

Key takeaway: discover → Macie; mask → dynamic masking.
Q000417:
Why this is correct:
KMS multi-Region keys share key material across Regions, so each Region can decrypt the other's data.

Why the other options are wrong:
• AWS managed keys: Regional.
• Single-Region key via IAM: can't decrypt elsewhere.
• Rotation: unrelated.

Key takeaway: cross-Region decryption → multi-Region keys.
Q000418:
Why this is correct:
CloudTrail Lake aggregates events across accounts and Regions into an event data store you query with SQL.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Logs Insights: not SQL across aggregated trails in this way.
• OpenSearch: requires ingestion.
• Config aggregator: configuration.

Key takeaway: SQL on CloudTrail events → CloudTrail Lake.
Q000419:
Why this is correct:
Athena can query CloudTrail logs already in S3 by defining a table (with partition projection), no pipeline needed.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Kinesis Analytics: streams.
• DataBrew: prep.
• Spectrum with ETL: unnecessary.

Key takeaway: CloudTrail in S3 → Athena.
Q000420:
Why this is correct:
Logs Insights queries logs stored in CloudWatch Logs. Athena queries data in S3, such as Parquet logs.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Athena can't query Parquet: it can.
• Logs Insights queries S3: no.
• Identical: no.

Key takeaway: where the data lives decides the tool.
Q000421:
Why this is correct:
PutObject and DeleteObject are data events. A trail logging only management events won't capture them.

Why the other options are wrong:
• CloudTrail can't log S3: it can.
• Encryption: unrelated.
• Trust policy: unrelated.

Key takeaway: object operations need data events.
Q000422:
Why this is correct:
An EventBridge rule matching the specific CloudTrail event triggers a notification (for example, SNS) in near real time.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Daily review: slow.
• Conformance pack alone: no notification.
• Log bucket encryption: unrelated.

Key takeaway: near-real-time alerts on API calls → EventBridge.
Q000425:
Why this is correct:
Macie finds PII in S3, and its findings can drive restrictions such as Lake Formation tags or permissions.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Config alone: no content discovery.
• Bucket policies alone: no discovery.
• CloudTrail Insights: API anomalies.

Key takeaway: discover PII, then restrict.
Q000427:
Why this is correct:
SCPs denying actions outside approved EU Regions prevent data from being stored elsewhere.

Why the other options are wrong:
• CloudTrail only: detective.
• Macie moves data: no.
• App checks only: bypassable.

Key takeaway: residency → SCP Region restrictions.
Q000428:
Why this is correct:
Project members access published data assets through their project's subscriptions and project roles, not personal broad permissions.

Why the other options are wrong:
• No shared assets: false.
• Account-wide admin: no.
• Unencrypted local copies: no.

Key takeaway: access via project subscriptions.
Q000429:
Why this is correct:
Business Unit A registers its data in Lake Formation and grants B's account cross-account access to specific tables.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Root credentials: never.
• Merge accounts: disruptive.
• Full dumps: duplication.

Key takeaway: cross-account data sharing → Lake Formation grants.
Q000430:
Why this is correct:
Config can't evaluate resources it isn't recording. Enable the recorder for S3 bucket resources.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Recreate bucket: no.
• Yearly evaluation: false.
• S3 unsupported: supported.

Key takeaway: no evaluations → check the recorder.
Q002151:
Why this is correct:
Firehose with record format conversion buffers JSON events, converts them to Parquet using a Glue schema, and delivers to S3 within minutes.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Custom KCL app: more code.
• One file per event: tiny files.
• Hourly Glue to CSV: slow and wrong format.

Key takeaway: stream to Parquet in S3 → Firehose conversion.
Q002152:
Why this is correct:
Errors on one shard mean a hot partition key. A higher-cardinality key, such as session ID, spreads writes across shards.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Synchronous calls: slower.
• More shards: the hot key still hits one shard.
• Retention: unrelated.

Key takeaway: one hot shard → better partition key.
Q002153:
Why this is correct:
Glue job bookmarks track processed files, so each run reads only new data.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Crawler: cataloging.
• Versioning: unrelated.
• More DPUs: still reprocesses.

Key takeaway: incremental processing → bookmarks.
Q002154:
Why this is correct:
Millions of tiny files add per-file overhead. Compacting into larger files (for example, 128 MB or more) speeds Athena queries.

Why the other options are wrong:
• More columns: no.
• Uncompressed JSON: slower.
• Longer timeout: no.

Key takeaway: small files → compaction.
Q002155:
Why this is correct:
MWAA runs existing Airflow DAGs as a managed service with minimal changes.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Scheduler with Lambda: rewrite.
• Glue workflows only: rewrite.
• Step Functions: rewrite 150 workflows.

Key takeaway: existing Airflow → MWAA.
Q002156:
Why this is correct:
DMS with a full load plus ongoing CDC continuously replicates inserts, updates, and deletes into S3.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Crawler: metadata.
• AppFlow: SaaS sources.
• Nightly dumps: no CDC.

Key takeaway: continuous DB changes → DMS CDC.
Q002157:
Why this is correct:
KEY distribution on order_id for both tables co-locates matching rows, avoiding redistribution during joins.

Why the other options are wrong:
• More sort keys: no collocation.
• ALL on large tables: huge storage.
• EVEN: redistribution.

Key takeaway: frequent large joins → shared distribution key.
Q002158:
Why this is correct:
Apache Iceberg tables support row-level deletes, so specific customers' records can be removed efficiently.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Object Lock: prevents deletion.
• Plain Parquet: rewrite files manually.
• CSV with manifest: no row-level deletes.

Key takeaway: row-level deletes in a data lake → Iceberg.
Q002159:
Why this is correct:
Configuring the crawler to combine compatible schemas (grouping behavior) creates a single table despite minor column differences.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Delete files: data loss.
• Run more often: same result.
• Different Region: no.

Key takeaway: one table from varied files → crawler grouping settings.
Q002160:
Why this is correct:
Redshift Spectrum external tables query historical data in S3 alongside hot data in Redshift, without loading it.

Why the other options are wrong:
• CSV for Excel: no.
• COPY all history: costly.
• DynamoDB: wrong store.

Key takeaway: hot in Redshift, cold in S3 → Spectrum.
Q002161:
Why this is correct:
The Glue Schema Registry enforces compatibility modes, so incompatible schema changes are rejected before breaking consumers.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Retention: unrelated.
• Single partition: throughput.
• Wiki: not enforcement.

Key takeaway: schema evolution control → Schema Registry.
Q002162:
Why this is correct:
Athena workgroups with per-query data usage limits (and workgroup limits) cap how much a team's queries can scan.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Requester Pays: S3 billing.
• Delete users: drastic.
• JSON: more scanning.

Key takeaway: control Athena spend → workgroup limits.
Q002163:
Why this is correct:
Glue Data Quality rules in DQDL inside the job can fail the pipeline when null rates exceed 1%, before loading.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Redshift rejects nulls: not automatically for this rule.
• More DPUs: unrelated.
• Manual checks: no automation.

Key takeaway: gate loads on data quality → Glue Data Quality.
Q002164:
Why this is correct:
A materialized view with auto refresh precomputes the aggregation, so the dashboard reads results quickly.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Faster refresh: more load.
• DISTSTYLE ALL on fact table: costly.
• Disable result caching: worse.

Key takeaway: repeated heavy aggregations → materialized views.
Q002165:
Why this is correct:
A few executors failing means data skew. Salt the skewed key or enable adaptive query execution skew-join handling.

Why the other options are wrong:
• More output files: no.
• CSV: no.
• More same-size executors: skewed partition still too big.

Key takeaway: skewed joins → salting or AQE.
Q002166:
Why this is correct:
Lake Formation LF-Tags with data filters give row-level (region) and column-level restrictions by business unit.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Separate table copies: duplication.
• IAM column lists: not supported for data.
• Bucket policies per prefix: no column control.

Key takeaway: row + column security in the lake → LF-Tags and data filters.
Q002167:
Why this is correct:
Redshift dynamic data masking policies attached to roles show masked card numbers to support staff and full values to authorized roles.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Shared decryption key: no protection.
• Concurrency scaling: performance.
• Nightly masked copy: stale and duplicated.

Key takeaway: role-based masking → dynamic data masking.
Q002168:
Why this is correct:
Redshift data sharing gives other accounts' clusters live, read-only access to curated data without copying.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Share admin password: insecure.
• DMS replication: copying.
• Nightly UNLOAD/COPY: stale.

Key takeaway: live cross-account sharing → Redshift data sharing.
Q002169:
Why this is correct:
A Glue security configuration specifies KMS keys for S3 output, CloudWatch Logs, and job bookmarks, applied to jobs.

Why the other options are wrong:
• SSL on connections: in transit only.
• Deny Glue: blocks work.
• Default S3 encryption only: doesn't cover logs or bookmarks.

Key takeaway: encrypt all Glue outputs → security configuration.
